reviews.text: Jiefangbei Street is one of the busiest and most vibrant areas in Chongqing. The atmosphere is lively, especially at night when the lights come on and the whole street feels energetic and modern. The Liberation Monument stands in the center, surrounded by shopping malls, restaurants, and street food stalls. There are plenty of shops — from international brands to local boutiques — making it a great place for shopping and people-watching. You can also find many hotpot restaurants and local snacks nearby, so it’s perfect for food lovers. Overall, Jiefangbei is a must-visit spot if you want to experience the city vibe of Chongqing — busy, bright, and full of life.

Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street is one of the most vibrant areas in Chongqing and a great place to really feel the city’s energy. The mix of modern skyscrapers, busy shopping streets, and constant flow of people makes it lively both day and night. There are plenty of food options nearby, from local snacks to restaurants and cafes, so it’s easy to spend hours just walking around, eating, and people-watching. At night, the lights and atmosphere make it even more impressive. If you want to experience the urban side of Chongqing and see how locals live, shop, and hang out, this is a must-visit spot.

If you want noodles, look for this specific stall and order their Top 1 on the menu. We've eaten at Bayi Food Hall 3 times already in 4 days. The selection of food, ample tables, and sparse crowds make it a great place to dine. You can walk to Bayi Food Hall from Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street. You can also get here by walking (eating) through Jiachangkou Food Street. The two are adjacent so it's a perfect location for a food crawl.

Visited Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street during my Chongqing trip and found it to be the bustling heart of the city. The area is a mix of modern skyscrapers, shopping malls, and local street vendors, making it a vibrant spot for both shopping and sightseeing. It’s a great place to experience the city’s energy, especially in the evening when the lights come alive. Walking along the street, you’ll find a mix of international brands, local shops, and eateries. While it’s very tourist-friendly, it still captures some local flavor in the small alleys branching off the main street. Street performers and neon signs add a lively atmosphere, perfect for photos. A few tips: it can get very crowded, so be prepared for a busy stroll. Also, while food options abound, many are aimed at tourists, so local recommendations are better if you’re looking for authentic Chongqing cuisine. Overall, Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street is great for sightseeing, shopping, and getting a feel of modern Chongqing, even if you skip the meals.

This is where the city’s energy never fades. By day, international brands like Louis Vuitton and Apple stand tall, and when the sun sets, a Blade Runner–style futuristic fantasy takes over. Neon billboards glow across almost every store at night, transforming the Liberation Monument into a futuristic lighthouse. Jie Fang Bei is also home to several vibrant food streets. I visited BaYi Yummy Street, where I indulged in skewers, spicy noodles, and refreshing desserts.

Chongqing's downtown commercial and business zone is dedicated to shopping malls, restaurants, entertainment venues and luxury hotels. There are several options available ranging from ordinary stores to brand name stores. Admire the towers and the lively atmosphere of the pedestrian streets lined with lights. The Jiefangbei Clock Tower was built to commemorate China's victory in the Sino-Japanese War.

Very vibrant, very beautiful and especially at night, it makes you feel like you have been transported out of China. The Jiefangbei monument is a must-see for Chongqing, and the fact that it's located right in the middle of the square is a great reminder of all the sacrifices that have been made and lives that were lost in order to make this hustle and bustle and vibrancy possible. Yela Mountain, also called Nujiang Mountain, is 4,618 meters above sea level. It is famous for its "ninety-nine turning turns" and is one of the more dangerous sections of the Sichuan-Tibet 318 Line. In addition, there is "Nujiang 72 Turn" in Yela Mountain, which refers to the winding road in Yela Mountain with an altitude of 4618 meters at the pass on the Sichuan-Tibet Line (located between Bangda Town and Basu County on the southern line of the Sichuan-Tibet Highway, 16 km) in Basu County, Qamdo Prefecture, Tibet [3], passing through the Nu River on the way, the steep slopes and dangerous roads are known as the "Ninety-nine Turns Back", the "108 Turns" of Yela Mountain, and the "99 Turns of Sichuan and Tibet". According to some statistics, there are actually more than 130 turns.

Esta imagen muestra una instalación artística ubicada en el distrito comercial de Jiefangbei, en la ciudad de Chongqing, China. Se encuentra en la zona peatonal de Jiefangbei (Monumento a la Liberación), un área emblemática de rascacielos y centros comerciales en Chongqing. La Obra se trata de una estructura de piedra que parece "levitar" sobre una hilera de pies humanos calzados con diversos tipos de zapatos (zapatos de cuero, zapatillas deportivas, tacones, etc.). Los caracteres grabados en la piedra están relacionados con el nombre de la zona ("解放碑步..." que se traduce como Monumento a la Liberación / Calle Peatonal). La instalación visualiza metafóricamente la idea de una ciudad o monumento sostenido por el paso y el esfuerzo de su gente.
